correctness.rationale: Finite commutative PIR ideals are exponent vectors over local chain factors. Their intersections are coordinatewise maxima, hence nonzero exactly when active supports intersect. For a two-set, total domination is therefore equivalent to support intersection plus full support union; singleton-support ideals prove necessity. Every qualifying pair is an edge and hence a paired dominating set. The existence boundary and the product-form count are then derived exactly. A standalone verifier confirms the classification on representative length boxes and direct Z/nZ ideal graphs.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete natural classification of minimum total and paired domination for every finite commutative PIR, not a single example. It identifies the exact structural obstructions, characterizes every minimum set by local support data, and gives a closed enumerator depending on all nilpotency lengths. For Z/nZ this yields an immediate prime-exponent formula, making the classification algebraically interpretable and reusable.
